messages:
sarah-sales: Heads up — FinLedger POC (EU regulated) needs strict EU-only residency and clear subprocessor visibility. Can someone confirm the exact behavior for hosted routing/pinning and whether we ever fail to non-EU regions? Also need: 1) can we pin tenant to specific EU region(s)? 2) canonical list of EU subprocessors + roles (processing vs. support) 3) policy for failover (automatic vs opt-in) 4) any pricing delta for EU-only reserved capacity or bursts out of region 5) TLS/mTLS & KMS/HSM options. Customer expects answers by Tue EOD. @mike-se can you lead?

mike-se: I can take point. Quick answers up front: we support tenant pinning at the routing policy level (region groups), and default hosted failover stays within EU if compatible regions exist. We do not route to non-EU regions unless explicitly allowed by policy. For strict no-egress, dedicated/private is recommended.

sarah-sales: ok thanks — customer may accept hosted if we can provide an enforceable routing policy + subproc list + contract addendum. They asked about a config example they can show their security team.

luis-eng: Example routing_policy we use for POCs (dev-friendly):

```
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "pin_regions": ["eu-central-1"],
    "preferred_failover": ["eu-west-1"],
    "allow_cross_region_fallback": false
  }
}
```

Notes: setting allow_cross_region_fallback:false prevents any non-EU fallback. If you set it true, fallback might go to another cloud region we control (could be non-EU) depending on capacity.

anita-security: Subprocessor list and roles: we keep an up-to-date list in the compliance portal (link shared privately). High-level: cloud infra providers (AWS/GCP in EU regions) = processing; CDN (Cloudflare) = metadata+edge routing; observability tools (Datadog/Prometheus/Splunk) = metrics (we offer EU tenancy for logs on request); incident/alerting vendors = support only; backups = encrypted and kept in-region unless customer opts in to cross-region DR. If they require DPA + SCCs, we can provide them.

anita-security: Important security caveat: cross-region failover will instantiate new runtime in the target region and rebuild KV/prefix caches — that can create transient reads from origin region for state hydration unless customer uses dedicated/private with explicit replication controls. For absolute no-egress, recommend Private.

oliver-legal: For contract: we can add an EU-only routing addendum and explicit subprocessor disclosure. We'll need the customer's exact definition of "EU-only" (e.g., do UK endpoints count?). Also confirm whether they require SCCs, DPA, and whether they require subprocessors to sign data localization commitments. Legal will draft an addendum; give us the customer's timeline.

kai-ps: Pricing: EU-only reserved capacity tends to be +~15–30% depending on region and GPU class; scarcity in certain EU zones drives the delta. Burst to global will be billed at global rates and may require cross-region egress costs. For POC we can offer a limited trial with EU-only infra and a temporary credit — I can draft a POC quote.

sarah-sales: customer question — what about UK fallbacks? They said GDPR requires EU/EEA, so UK is ambiguous. Thoughts?

mike-se: Practically: UK is separate from EU/EEA jurisdiction. If they require EU/EEA-only, do not include UK. Our routing_policy allows specifying exact region codes (eu-west-1/eu-central-1). If they want UK included, we can, but legal should confirm.

anita-security: If they're strict about EU/EEA, we should treat UK as non-EU. Also check whether they want encryption keys in customer-managed KMS (we support bringing-your-own-key for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports customer KMS for certain plans)

support-bot: Created support ticket #SL-14532 to export current EU subprocessor inventory and SLA notes.

mike-se: Proposed next steps: 1) I'll attach the subproc export and a one-page routing policy explainer. 2) Engineering to share the POC routing snippet (done). 3) Legal to start addendum draft (cc @oliver-legal). 4) Pricing to provide POC estimate & trial credit (cc @kai-ps). 5) Security to confirm any DR caveats (cc @anita-security). I'll follow up with the customer after we have the export.

anita-security: FYI — we had a customer who required an HSM-backed KMS + no cross-region backups; they moved to Private. If FinLedger's compliance bar is that high, recommend we position Private early.

kai-ps: I'll mock up 2 PO C scenarios: hosted EU-pinned (with routing addendum) and Dedicated (EU-only) with pricing diff. ETA EOD tomorrow for initial numbers.

sarah-sales: perfect. thanks everyone — I'll wait for the subproc export and the POC quote, then loop the customer in. :thumbsup:
